venue.name: Discover the Past Walking Tours
venue.description: Discover the Past Walking Tours is a family-run Victoria company founded by local historian John Adams that has offered guided walking tours of Victoria, British Columbia since the 1960s. Its tours include the year-round Ghostly Walks, daytime history walks, Chinatown Walks and tailored student tours for groups from preschool to post-grad, all led on foot around downtown Victoria.
venue.hours_notes: Most Ghostly Walks and History Walks begin outside the Visitor Information Centre at 812 Wharf Street; Chinatown Walks meet at the Bright Pearl Sculpture in the plaza near Fisgard and Government Streets. All bookings must be made online in advance of the tour start time.
venue.seasonal_notes: History walking tours run every day from the beginning of June until Labour Day and on weekends or by special arrangement the rest of the year. Ghostly Walks run every night in the summer season and the winter season page lists tours every night from November 3, 2025 to April 30, 2026. In December the Christmas in Old Victoria route starts in Bastion Square.
venue.price_year_or_season: FAQ page last modified 2026-02-13; prices described on the page as 'Current prices'.

programs.name: Student Tours (school groups)
programs.description: Tailored school walking tours: ghost tours, in-depth cultural adventures in Chinatown, White Jade Tiger, visite en francais, or a custom-tailored program. The company says it works with students of all ages from preschool to post-grad, can schedule tours at any time of day or night, and with enough notice can accommodate several classes at the same time. A special school-group rate is offered but the amount is not published; requests are made through the form on the student tours page, and 250-384-6698 is given for emergencies only.
programs.evidence: We offfer school groups a special rate that represents a significant savings over our normal per person fees.

programs.name: Ghostly Walks
programs.description: Guided evening walking tour of Victoria's ghost stories and true crime history. Ghostly Walks last 60 minutes and generally include 1.5-2 kilometres of walking around downtown Victoria. Public prices are Adults (18+) $24, Seniors (65+) $19, Students (12-17 or with a valid student card) $19, Children (6-11) $14, and kids 5 and under free; the site warns some content may not be suitable for young children. Tickets must be purchased online in advance. School groups get an unpublished discounted rate.
programs.evidence: Students (12-17 or with a valid student card): $19, Children (6-11): $14

programs.name: Victoria History Walks
programs.description: Daytime guided history walking tours weaving together the characters, landmarks and facts of Victoria's history, with routes criss-crossing downtown Victoria and other neighbourhoods. Historical tours last 90 minutes and generally include 2-3 kilometres of gentle walking. Public prices are Adults $24, Seniors $19, Students $19, Children (6-11) $14. In December the festive Christmas in Old Victoria route starts in Bastion Square. Tickets must be purchased online in advance.
programs.evidence: From the beginning of June until Labour Day, our historical walking tours run every day.

programs.name: Chinatown Walks
programs.description: Ninety-minute guided walk through Canada's oldest Chinatown covering history, culture, architecture and food, including Fan Tan Alley, traditional medicine shops and Canada's oldest Chinese temple. Public prices are Adults $24, Seniors $19, Students $19, Children (6-11) $14. Dogs are not permitted on this tour because it enters a venue that does not allow them. Tours meet at the Bright Pearl Sculpture across from the Gate of Harmonious Interest near Fisgard and Government Streets.
programs.evidence: Chinatown Walks take place year-round on Saturdays at 10:30 am (except Christmas and New Year's Day)

gaps: The school-group rate is described as 'a special rate that represents a significant savings' but the actual amount is never published; a director must request a quote through the form.
No minimum lead time is given for student tours, only 'with enough notice we are able to accomodate several classes at the same time'.
No maximum or minimum group size per guide is stated.

No youngest age is stated. The site says it works with students 'from preschool to post-grad' but also warns that some Ghostly Walks content might not be suitable for young children, and the public child fare band starts at age 6.
No booking email address is published; contact is via web form plus 250-384-6698 which the student tours page says is for emergencies only.
No rain backup: these are outdoor walking tours and the site does not say what happens in bad weather or if a tour is cancelled.
No washroom or lunch space information; tours are on-street and start at outdoor meeting points.
No wheelchair or stroller accessibility information for any route, only that tours involve 1.5-3 km of walking.
No bus drop-off or parking guidance at the meeting points.
No adult chaperone ratio or whether accompanying teachers pay.
The Ghostly Walks and Private Tours pages advertise 'Live Zoom Tours' and 'Watch Anytime Tours' as 'Not Currently Available', so no virtual option is bookable.

The homepage schedule/calendar and the ticket prices are served through FareHarbor, an off-site booking partner, so live dates and any group discount codes could not be read on the venue's own domain.

The Ghostly Walks and History Tours pages contain no photographs of their own in the fetched text - only tour logos, decorative arrow SVGs, embedded Vimeo videos and a guide portrait - so the images for those two programs were taken from the labelled tour cards on the homepage instead of from the tour pages. The Open Graph image on every interior page, including the student tours page, is the guide headshot 'Jason-Portait.jpg', which was skipped as a staff portrait; the student tours page has no photo, so that program has no image.
The booking calendar and any tour photography inside it are embedded from FareHarbor, so no images could be taken from the schedule.
